training_summary: The corpus reveals that Roman Republic scientific achievements were primarily practical and engineering-focused, with limited pure theoretical science. The seed corpus emphasizes civil engineering (sanitation, aqueducts) and monarchical governance transitions, but lacks comprehensive coverage of Roman scientific methodology, natural philosophy, or key figures like Pliny, Vitruvius, and medical practitioners.

key_works.facet_contribution: Demonstrates Roman practical scientific approach through archaeological evidence of sophisticated sanitation systems, water management, and public health engineering
Shows emergence of systematic legal methodology in late Republic, representing Roman approach to systematizing knowledge domains
Illustrates Roman surveying and urban planning science through Campus Martius development and spatial organization techniques

insights.label: Pliny the Elder
insights.evidence: Referenced in worldhistory.org overview as key Roman scientific author. Wikidata confirms Natural History (Q442) as major work. Perseus Digital Library shows 37-book Natural History covering astronomy, geography, zoology, botany, mineralogy, and medicine.
insights.reasoning: Pliny represents the culmination of Roman encyclopedic natural philosophy approach, systematizing Greek and indigenous knowledge

insights.label: Vitruvius
insights.evidence: Worldhistory.org overview identifies Vitruvius as key Roman architectural theorist. Roman Engineering Wikipedia article references De Architectura as foundational engineering text combining theory with practice.
insights.reasoning: Vitruvius systematized architectural and engineering knowledge, representing Roman approach to technical science

insights.label: Engineering-Military Integration
insights.evidence: Roman Engineering Wikipedia shows military applications of civil engineering (roads, bridges, siege equipment). Campus Martius work demonstrates military training ground development using surveying science.
insights.reasoning: Roman scientific advances were deeply integrated with military needs, creating cross-facet dependencies

insights.label: Pedanius Dioscorides
insights.evidence: Wikidata search identified Dioscorides as Roman-period pharmacist. Roman medicine Wikipedia confirms he was Roman army physician who systematized botanical medicine.
insights.reasoning: Dioscorides represents Roman systematic approach to medical botany and pharmacology

candidate_assessments.label: quartuncia
candidate_assessments.evidence: Wikidata shows this is a unit of mass/denomination - currency measure rather than scientific concept. Belongs in economic facet covering weights, measures, and monetary systems.

candidate_assessments.label: bes
candidate_assessments.evidence: Wikidata shows this is a currency/denomination/unit of mass - monetary and measurement unit rather than scientific concept. Should be handled by economic facet.

discovered_works.facet_contribution: Comprehensive treatment of Greco-Roman scientific traditions and their anchoring in cultural context

discovered_works.title: Materialising the Roman Empire
discovered_works.facet_contribution: Material culture approaches to understanding Roman technological and scientific practices

discovered_works.title: Notes and Further Reading
discovered_works.facet_contribution: Bibliography covering Pliny and Roman natural philosophy traditions

decomposition_assessment.reason: Scientific aspects of Roman Republic represent a coherent but limited domain focused on practical applications. Six main sub-domains identified (engineering, medicine, natural philosophy, mathematics/astronomy, agriculture, military technology) with estimated 8-10 concepts each, totaling ~50 concepts under the threshold of 60.

corpus_gaps: Primary sources from key figures (Pliny Natural History, Vitruvius De Architectura, Varro Res Rusticae)
Theoretical vs practical science debates in Roman culture
Transfer of Hellenistic scientific knowledge to Rome

fischer_checks.note: Avoided claiming to represent 'the whole' of Roman science, acknowledged gaps and limited corpus coverage
Identified military needs as one factor among others (economic, political, cultural) driving Roman technical innovation

digital_principles_applied.note: Acknowledged that OpenAlex searches returned limited results, indicating possible bias toward modern rather than ancient scientific topics
Multiple connection timeouts to OAPEN and Perseus affected research depth; documented these access limitations

repertoire_patterns.evidence: Pliny, Vitruvius, and Dioscorides served as knowledge brokers, systematizing and transmitting Greek scientific knowledge to Roman practitioners

temporal_anchors.label: Roman Republic period
temporal_anchors.evidence: Corpus focus on Republican period scientific developments before Imperial systematization

geographic_anchors.evidence: Central locus for scientific knowledge concentration and practical application
Source region for Hellenistic scientific traditions adopted by Romans

claim.text: Roman scientific methodology prioritized practical applications over theoretical speculation, as seen in engineering, medicine, and natural history compilations.
Roman aqueduct technology represented sophisticated hydraulic engineering combining empirical observation with mathematical calculation for gradient management.
